Question: In the MVC architectural pattern, what is a main advantage of separating the Model from the View?
Answer 1: The same data can be shown in different ways without changing the model
Answer 2: The system always runs faster because it has fewer classes
Answer 3: The View can change the data directly, without a Controller
Answer 4: The user interface no longer needs to be tested
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: data is independent of its presentation; the same data can have several views.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns; java-design-patterns.com - Model-View-Controller (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/model-view-controller/)

Question: What is a known disadvantage of the Layered (n-tier) architecture?
Answer 1: A request may pass through several layers, which can reduce performance
Answer 2: A layer cannot be replaced even when its interface stays the same
Answer 3: Every component must talk directly to the database
Answer 4: It cannot be used in desktop applications
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantage: performance overhead from layer interaction. Advantage: a layer can be replaced if its interface is kept.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Layered Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/layered-architecture/); Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: In a client-server architecture, what is a typical disadvantage?
Answer 1: Each service is a single point of failure, and performance depends on the network
Answer 2: Clients and servers must run on the same computer
Answer 3: Adding a server requires changing the hardware of every client
Answer 4: Clients cannot use shared services such as printing
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantages: single point of failure, network-dependent performance. Advantage: servers can be distributed across a network.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: In the Repository architecture, components share data only through a central repository. What is a disadvantage of this design?
Answer 1: Components must know about every other component in the system
Answer 2: The repository is a single point of failure, so a problem in it affects the whole system
Answer 3: Data cannot be backed up in one place
Answer 4: Components must send data directly to each other
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantage: single point of failure; hard to distribute. Advantage: components are independent and data is managed consistently in one place.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: What is a disadvantage of the Pipe and Filter architecture?
Answer 1: Adding a new transformation (filter) to the system is very difficult
Answer 2: Filters can never run at the same time
Answer 3: Filters must agree on a data format, and each filter must parse its input and format its output
Answer 4: Data must flow in both directions between every pair of filters
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantage: agreed data format and parsing overhead. Advantages: easy to understand, easy to add transformations, sequential or concurrent.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: In which situation can MVC be a poor choice?
Answer 1: When the same data must be shown in several different views
Answer 2: When several developers work on different parts of the system in parallel
Answer 3: When the user interface changes often
Answer 4: In a very small and simple application, because it adds setup complexity and extra code
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: extra code and complexity when the data model and interactions are simple.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Model-View-Controller (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/model-view-controller/); Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: In an Event-Driven Architecture, producers publish events and consumers react to them. What is a main trade-off of this architecture?
Answer 1: Adding a new event consumer requires changing all event producers
Answer 2: The flow of the system is hard to trace and debug, because components are loosely coupled and asynchronous
Answer 3: It cannot handle loads that change over time
Answer 4: Each producer must wait until every consumer has finished
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: hard to track and debug; depends on messaging. Advantages: scalability, new consumers added with little impact.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Event-Driven Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/event-driven-architecture/)

Question: What is the main advantage of the Hexagonal (Ports and Adapters) architecture?
Answer 1: It needs fewer abstractions than any other architecture
Answer 2: It is the simplest choice for very small applications
Answer 3: The core business logic can be tested and changed independently of the UI, the database and external services
Answer 4: The user interface talks directly to the database, which saves time
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantages: testability, flexibility, maintainability. Trade-offs: more abstractions; may be over-engineering for simple applications.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Hexagonal Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/hexagonal-architecture/)

Question: Eclipse is built as a small runtime core (based on OSGi), and most of its functionality is provided by plug-ins. What is the main advantage of this plug-in architecture?
Answer 1: All features are compiled into one module, so nothing needs to be loaded at run time
Answer 2: Plug-ins cannot depend on each other, so there are never version problems
Answer 3: The core contains all the business logic, so plug-ins are not needed for main features
Answer 4: New features can be added as plug-ins without changing the core
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: extensibility - features are added as plug-ins around a small core. Trade-off: managing plug-in dependencies and loading.
Source: Kim Moir, "Eclipse", in The Architecture of Open Source Applications, Vol. 1 (aosabook.org); Eclipse Platform documentation, "What is Eclipse?" (help.eclipse.org)

Question: In a microservices architecture, the system is split into small services that are deployed independently and each manage their own data. What is a main disadvantage of this architecture?
Answer 1: All services must be written in the same programming language
Answer 2: The system becomes distributed: remote calls are slow and may fail, and keeping data consistent across services is harder
Answer 3: Changing one service always requires redeploying the whole system
Answer 4: Each service must be scaled together with all the other services	2
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantages: distribution, eventual consistency and operational complexity. Advantages: independent deployment, strong module boundaries, freedom to use different technologies.
Source: Martin Fowler, Microservice Trade-Offs (https://martinfowler.com/articles/microservice-trade-offs.html); James Lewis and Martin Fowler, Microservices (https://martinfowler.com/articles/microservices.html)

Question: In a peer-to-peer (P2P) architecture, every node (peer) can both provide and use services. Compared with client-server, what is a main advantage?
Answer 1: All data is kept on one central server, so it is always consistent
Answer 2: It is easier to secure, because one server controls who can access the data
Answer 3: There is no central server, so work and storage are spread over many computers and the failure of one peer does not stop the system
Answer 4: Peers never need to communicate with each other
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: decentralised - uses the computing power and storage of many networked computers, with no single central server. Disadvantage: harder to secure and manage, because there is no central control.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 17 Distributed Software Engineering - Architectural patterns for distributed systems (peer-to-peer)

Question: In MVC, which component is mainly responsible for handling user actions and coordinating updates?
Answer 1: The Controller
Answer 2: The Model only
Answer 3: The database server
Answer 4: The operating system
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: separates user interaction from data and presentation; trade-off: additional coordination and components.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns; java-design-patterns.com - Model-View-Controller (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/model-view-controller/)

Question: Why can a layered architecture make a system easier to maintain?
Answer 1: All layers must use the same programming language
Answer 2: Every layer can directly modify every other layer
Answer 3: Responsibilities are separated, so a layer can change while its interface remains stable
Answer 4: The system does not need interfaces
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: separation of responsibilities and replaceability; trade-off: inter-layer overhead.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Layered Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/layered-architecture/); Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: What is the primary role of a server in a client-server architecture?
Answer 1: To eliminate all communication over the network
Answer 2: To provide shared services or resources in response to client requests
Answer 3: To guarantee that all clients use the same operating system
Answer 4: To make clients store every copy of the database
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: centralised provision of services; trade-off: server availability and network dependence.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: In a Pipe and Filter architecture, what does a filter typically do?
Answer 1: Stores the final result as the only shared database
Answer 2: Sends all input directly to the user interface
Answer 3: Controls which players can enter the system
Answer 4: Transforms input data and passes the result to the next processing stage
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: decomposes data processing into reusable stages; trade-off: agreed data formats.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: What is a key advantage of a central repository architecture?
Answer 1: Components can share and access data through a common store
Answer 2: The repository can never become unavailable
Answer 3: Every component must maintain a separate copy of all data
Answer 4: Components do not need a shared data format
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: easier data sharing and management; disadvantage: central failure or performance bottleneck.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: What is an event consumer in an Event-Driven Architecture?
Answer 1: A component that must start every event producer
Answer 2: A database that stores only user passwords
Answer 3: A component that reacts when a relevant event is published
Answer 4: A component that converts every event into a synchronous request
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: loose coupling between producers and consumers; trade-off: asynchronous flows can be hard to debug.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Event-Driven Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/event-driven-architecture/)

Question: How is new functionality commonly added to a microkernel (plug-in) architecture?
Answer 1: By rewriting the operating system for each feature
Answer 2: By adding a plug-in that extends a small core
Answer 3: By placing all new features directly in one large core class
Answer 4: By preventing third-party modules from loading
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: extensibility of a small core; trade-off: dependency and version management.
Source: Kim Moir, "Eclipse", in The Architecture of Open Source Applications, Vol. 1 (aosabook.org); Eclipse Platform documentation, "What is Eclipse?" (help.eclipse.org)

Question: A request crosses many layers before reaching the database. What is a possible architectural cost?
Answer 1: Every layer must run on a different physical computer
Answer 2: The application automatically becomes peer-to-peer
Answer 3: Data can no longer be validated
Answer 4: Additional calls and processing between layers may increase response time
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantage: performance overhead across layer boundaries; advantage: modular maintenance.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Layered Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/layered-architecture/); Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: A client-server application slows down because many clients use one server. Which issue best explains this?
Answer 1: The server may become a performance bottleneck under high load
Answer 2: Clients cannot send requests over a network
Answer 3: Every client must automatically become a new server
Answer 4: The architecture forbids multiple simultaneous users
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantage: central server may limit scalability; advantage: shared service management.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: A team wants to test business rules without opening the graphical interface. Which MVC property helps most?
Answer 1: The View is allowed to contain all business logic
Answer 2: The Controller must store every database record
Answer 3: Business logic in the Model can be exercised independently of the View
Answer 4: Each screen must duplicate its own data model
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: separation supports testability; trade-off: more components and coordination.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns; java-design-patterns.com - Model-View-Controller (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/model-view-controller/)

Question: A system cleans logs, converts formats and then calculates statistics. Why might Pipe and Filter suit this workflow?
Answer 1: Every processing stage must share mutable global state
Answer 2: The processing can be split into ordered transformations with explicit inputs and outputs
Answer 3: Each filter must open a graphical window
Answer 4: All filters must be compiled into a single method
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: clear composable transformations; trade-off: input and output format agreement.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: Which challenge is more typical of peer-to-peer systems than of systems with a single central server?
Answer 1: They cannot use network connections
Answer 2: Every peer must use one physical disk
Answer 3: Only one peer is allowed to send requests
Answer 4: Coordinating security and data availability across independent peers can be harder
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Disadvantage: distributed security and management; advantage: no single central service provider.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 17 Distributed Software Engineering - Architectural patterns for distributed systems (peer-to-peer)

Question: An Eclipse plug-in stops loading after the platform is upgraded. Which plug-in architecture trade-off does this illustrate?
Answer 1: Plug-ins are never allowed to use interfaces
Answer 2: Version and dependency compatibility between plug-ins and the core must be managed
Answer 3: The system must become a client-server application
Answer 4: Adding new features always requires rewriting the entire core
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: maintaining extension compatibility; advantage: adding features without changing the core.
Source: Kim Moir, "Eclipse", in The Architecture of Open Source Applications, Vol. 1 (aosabook.org); Eclipse Platform documentation, "What is Eclipse?" (help.eclipse.org)

Question: Two microservices update separate databases during one business operation. What makes this more difficult than a single-database transaction?
Answer 1: All microservices are required to run in the same process
Answer 2: Service boundaries remove the need for network communication
Answer 3: Coordinating failures and consistency across independently owned data stores is complex
Answer 4: An API can never be used between microservices
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: distributed data consistency and failure handling; advantage: independent deployment.
Source: Martin Fowler, Microservice Trade-Offs (https://martinfowler.com/articles/microservice-trade-offs.html); James Lewis and Martin Fowler, Microservices (https://martinfowler.com/articles/microservices.html)

Question: An event producer publishes an order-created event, and several independent consumers react later. Which consequence should the team anticipate?
Answer 1: The producer must wait for all consumers before it can finish
Answer 2: Every consumer automatically executes in one deterministic order
Answer 3: The producer must know the source code of each consumer
Answer 4: Processing may be asynchronous, making execution order and debugging harder to follow
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: event ordering and tracing across asynchronous consumers; advantage: loose coupling.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Event-Driven Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/event-driven-architecture/)

Question: A team replaces a database implementation but wants to keep its business rules unchanged. Which design best follows Ports and Adapters?
Answer 1: Business logic depends on a port interface, and a database adapter implements that interface
Answer 2: Business logic calls the database vendor's API everywhere
Answer 3: The user interface must directly modify every database table
Answer 4: Database logic and business rules are placed in the same screen class
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Advantage: business logic remains independent of external technology; trade-off: additional abstraction.
Source: java-design-patterns.com - Hexagonal Architecture (https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/hexagonal-architecture/)

Question: Several independent components depend on one shared repository. Which architecture risk follows from this centralisation?
Answer 1: The components cannot exchange any information
Answer 2: Repository failure or overload may affect many components at once
Answer 3: Every component must store a different version of the schema
Answer 4: The repository automatically guarantees zero network latency
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: central failure or performance bottleneck; advantage: common data access.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: Which requirement is least suited to a simple Pipe and Filter architecture?
Answer 1: A pipeline that converts file formats in sequence
Answer 2: Independent stages that transform text
Answer 3: Components that require frequent two-way coordination and tightly shared mutable state
Answer 4: A sequence that cleans and validates imported records
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: interdependent components fit poorly with simple one-way data-flow stages.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 6 "Architectural Design", section 6.3 Architectural patterns

Question: A team chooses a peer-to-peer design to avoid depending on one central server. Which trade-off should it explicitly plan for?
Answer 1: All requests must still pass through one mandatory central server
Answer 2: Peers can never join or leave the network
Answer 3: A peer-to-peer network removes all data consistency concerns
Answer 4: Distributed discovery, trust and coordination can become more difficult
Advantages / disadvantages covered: Trade-off: distributed discovery, security and coordination; advantage: decentralised resources.
Source: Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering, 10th ed., Chapter 17 Distributed Software Engineering - Architectural patterns for distributed systems (peer-to-peer)
